text: Q: When is rent due and how can a resident pay? A: Rent is due on the 1st of each month. There is a grace period through the 5th; rent received after the 5th is late. Residents can pay through the Mira resident portal by bank transfer or card, or enroll in AutoPay to have rent drawn automatically on the 1st. Always quote the resident's exact balance and due date from their account record; never estimate an amount.

Q: What is the late fee policy? A: If rent is not received by the end of the grace period on the 5th, a late fee of 50 dollars applies, plus 10 dollars per day after the 10th, up to a cap of 100 dollars per month. A first-time late fee may be waived once per 12 months for residents in good standing. Late rent that remains unpaid past the 10th may begin the notice process per the lease and local law.

Q: How does a resident submit a maintenance request? A: Routine maintenance requests (a dripping faucet, a loose handle, an appliance issue) are logged as a work order and a technician is scheduled, typically within two to three business days. Describe the issue and the location in the unit. For anything urgent or after hours, see the emergency policy. Mira confirms every work order by text with a tracking number.

Q: What counts as a maintenance emergency and what should a resident do? A: Emergencies are issues that threaten safety or cause active property damage: a major water leak or flooding, no heat in freezing weather, a gas smell, a total power outage, an overflowing sewage backup, or being locked out. For a gas smell, leave the unit immediately and call the gas company and 911 first, then Mira. For a water leak, shut off the water at the valve and report it as an emergency so a technician is dispatched right away rather than scheduled. Emergencies are handled 24/7.

Q: Where is the water shutoff and how do you stop a leak? A: Each unit has a main water shutoff valve, usually under the kitchen sink or near the water heater; turn it clockwise to stop the flow. Individual fixtures have their own shutoff valves behind or below them. For a leak, shut off the nearest valve first to limit damage, move belongings away from the water, and report it as an emergency work order so a technician is dispatched.

Q: Who is responsible for repairs, the landlord or the resident? A: The landlord is responsible for maintaining the structure, plumbing, electrical, heating, and supplied appliances in working order, and for habitability. The resident is responsible for damage they or their guests cause beyond normal wear and tear, for keeping the unit clean, and for replacing consumables like light bulbs and smoke-detector batteries. When responsibility is unclear, log the work order and Mira will assess on site; charges only apply for resident-caused damage and are disclosed first.

Q: How does the security deposit work and when is it returned? A: The security deposit is held for the term of the lease. After move-out, it is returned within the period required by local law (commonly 14 to 30 days) minus any lawful deductions for unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear. Normal wear and tear cannot be deducted. An itemized statement of any deductions is provided with the refund. Cleaning and painting for ordinary use are generally the landlord's cost, not deductions.

Q: How does lease renewal work? A: Mira sends a renewal offer about 60 days before the lease end date. A resident can renew for another term, switch to month-to-month where offered (often at a higher rate), or give notice to vacate. If no action is taken by the lease end, the lease may convert to month-to-month per its terms. Any rent change at renewal is stated in the offer and is subject to local rent regulations where they apply.

Q: Can a resident break their lease early? A: Breaking a lease early generally requires written notice and may involve an early-termination fee or responsibility for rent until the unit is re-rented, as stated in the lease. Some situations are protected by law (for example active military deployment, or unsafe/uninhabitable conditions) and may allow termination without penalty. Mira will work with the resident on options such as a lease transfer or finding a replacement resident.

Q: What is the policy on subletting and long-term guests? A: Subletting requires prior written approval from Mira; the proposed subtenant must apply and be screened, and the original resident usually remains responsible under the lease. Guests staying longer than 14 consecutive days may be considered unauthorized occupants and must be added to the lease. Short visits are fine and need no approval.

Q: What are the community rules around noise, pets, and parking? A: Quiet hours are 10 PM to 7 AM; keep noise low so it does not disturb neighbors. Pets require an approved pet addendum and any applicable pet deposit or rent; service and assistance animals are not pets and are accommodated per law. Each unit has its assigned parking space or permit; guest parking is in marked visitor spots only, and unauthorized vehicles may be towed.

Q: What is the move-out process? A: Give written notice per the lease (commonly 30 to 60 days before the end date). Schedule a move-out inspection, return all keys and remotes, and leave the unit broom-clean with personal belongings removed. The security deposit, minus any lawful deductions, is returned with an itemized statement within the legally required window. Forwarding address should be provided so the refund can be sent.
